brief:
Tonight is Legs A, and it is the first leg session you have run in ten days. Legs B never happened on the 27th — you ran Push A instead — so your legs are the freshest thing you own right now, and that is why nearly everything moves up tonight. The leg press opener goes from 180 to 200, because you finished ten reps at 180 last time and 200 is the smallest step that machine makes. The top set stays at 240: both trainers agreed on that ceiling, so do not go hunting for 260. The leg curl runs all four sets at 142.5 after you hit fifteen there on the 20th. Calves, extensions, hips and crunches each go up by a single rep at the same weight, which is the smallest honest move there is.

Now the part I owe you. You have written four questions to this program in eleven days and got no answer to any of them. Here they are, answered.

On 16 August you asked whether four sets of leg curls on RDL day was too much hamstring work. It was, and it is fixed — but on Legs B, the day that actually has the RDL, which is the day you asked about. Legs A has no RDL, and you accepted four sets here yourself on 20 August. So tonight's four sets are not the thing you questioned.

On 28 August you asked why face pulls are three sets on Pull A when you think two is right, and then you did two. There is a card for it tonight. Pull B already runs two. Say yes and Pull A matches.

On 17 August you asked why there are no corrective exercises anywhere in the program. I cannot put that one on a card, and I would rather tell you why than let it go quiet for a third time: every core set you have bends you forward, and there is no anti-rotation movement — nothing like a Pallof press — anywhere in the app's 37-exercise list. It cannot be prescribed until that list itself is changed. That is a change to the app, not to your plan, and it needs your word.

One question back to you. Push A on the 27th ran 37 minutes and stopped after a single set of overhead triceps, where the same session took 56 minutes on the 17th. I have not built anything on that, because I do not know whether you ran out of time or ran out of gas. Tell me which and I will use it.

flags.note: Legs B was skipped on 27 August — you ran Push A instead — so tonight is your first leg session since 20 August, ten days ago.
Your 16 August leg curl question is answered on Legs B, the day with the RDL that you actually asked about; the four sets tonight are on Legs A, which you accepted yourself on 20 August.
Your 28 August face pull question is a card tonight: Pull A drops to the two sets you did and already runs on Pull B.

Still open, and still not something I can put on a card: there is no anti-rotation core movement anywhere in the app's 37-exercise list, so the corrective work you asked about on 17 August cannot be prescribed until that list is changed. Say the word and it gets added.

Push A on 27 August ran 37 minutes and ended after one set of overhead triceps, against 56 minutes for the same session on 17 August — I have not changed any number because of it, and I would like to know whether that was the clock or your legs.
The two rep-range cards do not contradict tonight's numbers: tonight runs the range you have now, and if you accept them the next Legs A opens lower with the weight moving instead of the reps.
Meso 2, week 1 of 4, a build block — this is the part of the cycle where work goes on, not off.

proposals.why: Your leg curl asks twelve to fifteen reps on Legs A but ten to twelve on Legs B, and it is the same machine at the same 142.5 on both — on 20 August your best Legs A set was thirteen, which is inside the range but not the top, so the weight can never move, while the identical 142.5 for twelve on Legs B on 16 August is the top of its range and earns the next step; this makes Legs A ten to twelve so the only hamstring work on that day can actually progress.

The cable crunch asks twelve to fifteen and you finished at thirteen on Legs A and twelve on Legs B, both at 60 lb, so the stack has nothing that can ever move it — and unlike the hanging leg raise, which carries no weight and needs the high range you accepted, this one is loaded, so ten to twelve makes the twelves you already do earn the next plate.

Same change on the other leg day, and they belong together — the Legs B cable crunch sits at the same 60 lb and finished at twelve on 16 August, so leaving it at twelve to fifteen would freeze it on one day while the other one climbs.

You asked on 28 August why Pull A calls for three face pull sets when you think two is right, and you did two that night — Pull B already runs two, so this makes the two days agree with each other and with you.

overrides.reason: You finished ten reps at 180 last time, which is the top of the range, and 200 is the smallest step this machine makes; the top set stays at 240 because both trainers agreed that is your ceiling tonight.
The weight stays at 17.5 because nine, nine and eight never reached the top of the range and the next dumbbell up is 20, which is too big a jump to have earned.
You hit fifteen at 142.5 on 20 August, so the whole slot moves to 142.5 tonight instead of opening light at 127.5.
Both sets stopped at thirteen inside a twelve to fifteen range, so tonight asks for the reps before it asks for more weight.
Twelve and twelve is the floor of the range, so this steps by one rep at the same weight.
Thirteen and thirteen sits mid-range, so one more rep each; fifteens are what buy the next step up.
One more rep on each set at the same 300, because the next pin on this machine is 320 and that is too big a jump from thirteen, thirteen and twelve.
Three flat thirteens with no drop-off on the last set, so this asks fourteen; the small micro plate waits until you are finishing fifteens.

dissent.progression: Opener up to 200 with the back sets taking a rep each — 200x10, 220x10, 240x9 — because ten at 180 topped the range.
dissent.recovery: Repeat 20 August exactly — 180x10, 220x9, 240x8 — holding a 240 ceiling and adding nothing.
dissent.why: The two seats actually agree on the thing that matters most: 240 is the ceiling tonight and neither of them wants 260. What they split on is the opener, and there progression is plainly right. He finished ten reps at 180, which is the top of an eight-to-ten range, and the leg press moves in 20-lb steps, so 200 is not an aggressive raise — it is the only raise available, and repeating 180 is exactly the silent copy-paste the progression seat exists to catch. Recovery's grounds were the rest-drift it saw climbing across the last three sessions, and that trend is real, but it is a Push and Pull trend: Legs B was skipped on 27 August, so he has not trained legs since 20 August. Ten days is the longest gap he has had, and it lands on the freshest muscle group he owns in week 1 of a build block. Recovery filed no veto and said itself that the brake it wanted was the 240 ceiling rather than a stop — it has that ceiling. I took progression whole, weight for weight.

dissent.progression: Four sets, all at 142.5 — 14, 13, 13, 12 — after fifteen reps at that weight on 20 August.
dissent.recovery: Three sets of 142.5 for twelve, cutting the fourth set on the grounds of his written hamstring-volume question.
dissent.why: Recovery is reading a real signal and pointing it at the wrong day, and I can see that only because I can see a file it cannot. His 16 August question was specifically about four sets of leg curls on the same day as the RDL — that is Legs B. Tonight is Legs A, which has no RDL in it. More decisive: on 20 August, four days after he asked, he was given a card that set Legs A to four sets and Legs B to three, and he accepted it. He answered his own question with a tap, and cutting Legs A now would be overriding his own decision in the name of honouring it. The load is also earned outright — fifteen reps at 142.5 on the 20th is the top of the range at that weight. Recovery's underlying point, that his written questions get ignored, is correct and important, so I have answered all four of them by name in the brief rather than burying the concern in a set count.

dissent.progression: 300 for 14, 14, 13 — one rep on each set, holding the weight because the next pin is 320.
dissent.why: Recovery asked for less than he already did. On 20 August he logged thirteen, thirteen and twelve; twelve, twelve and twelve is a step backwards, and it came with no pain finding, no injury finding and no veto behind it. A brake that reverses completed work needs grounds, and there were none offered here beyond general fatigue, which does not apply to a muscle he has not trained in ten days. Progression's move is the smallest one available — one rep, same weight — and it is right that 320 would be too big a jump. Taken whole.
